text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty HIGH - gpu-oom spike detected on cuda-cluster-3. 18 pods OOMKilled in the last 6m. Alert group: gpu-memory-pressure. PD: https://pd.example/incidents/INC-7890

pagerduty: Incident INC-7890 triggered, notifying escalation policy: eng-oncall.

sam (oncall): acked. oncall taking. starting rapid triage. tagging @maria @kai

maria (sre): on it. quick ask: is this one model or many? looks like multiple heavy-replay jobs ramped yesterday.

kai (ml-infra): initial check: top pods by OOMs: model-replay-v2-*, batcher-queue-0, realtime-infer-3. GPU mem usage hitting 100% then OOM. running nvidia-smi on node gpu-node-14 now.

ops-bot: Deploy pipeline detected a canary yesterday at 03:12 UTC to cuda-cluster-3 (deploy/replica-set model-replay-v2 -> image: inference:v2.7).

sam (oncall): getting `kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide` output. Found 12 pods in CrashLoopBackOff (OOMKilled).

maria (sre): immediate mitigation options: 1) temporarily scale down replay batchers 2) reduce per-request batch_size via runtime flag 3) cordon and drain worst nodes and spin up warm nodes in different AZ. Recommend 1+2 for fastest impact.

jamal (prod-eng): if we reduce batcher concurrency, throughput drops but latency stays sane. we should notify affected customers if we do aggressive throttling.

kai (ml-infra): quick commands:
```bash
# check GPU usage history
kubectl exec -n inference gpu-node-14 -- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv -l
# list recent OOM events
kubectl get events -n inference --field-selector reason=OOMKilled --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -n 30
```

maria (sre): logs showing repeated allocation failures: here is truncated stack from realtime-infer-3-7dfc:
```
2026-02-18T03:40:12Z ERROR cuda: out of memory when allocating 33554432 bytes
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/infer/runner.py", line 412, in forward
    ctx = torch.cuda.current_stream().record_event()
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. tried to allocate 32MiB
```

sam (oncall): implemented mitigation: scaled batcher replicas down from 16 -> 4 and set env INFER_MAX_BATCH=8 on batcher config. issuing rollout now.

ops-bot: Applying patch to deployment/batcher-queue-0: `kubectl patch deployment/batcher-queue-0 -n inference --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/replicas","value":4}]'`

maria (sre): also updating runtime config for realtime service to set --max-batch-size=8 via feature flag. will monitor OOM rate.

pagerduty: INC-7890 acknowledged by sam (oncall).

kai (ml-infra): quick health checks post mitigation: GPU memory usage per pod dropping from peak ~14.9Gi -> ~11-12Gi. OOM events 6m window: before=18, after=2. still see one noisy node (gpu-node-14).

sam (oncall): cordoned gpu-node-14 and drained non-critical pods; starting node reboot to clear hung allocations.

ops-bot: Node gpu-node-14 cordon: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-14`
ops-bot: Draining non-daemonset pods: `kubectl drain gpu-node-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

maria (sre): customer impact check: affect surface = realtime infer for small subset of customers (approx 4 customers) seeing increased 5xx and elevated latency. batch replay jobs paused partially. Not a full outage but degraded for some.

jamal (prod-eng): pinging account managers for the 4 customers and rounding up a brief status note. suggested customer message draft: "We detected resource pressure affecting real-time inference on a subset of requests; we have reduced batch concurrency and are restoring capacity. We'll follow up with a timeline once stabilized."

sam (oncall): sent note to AMs.

kai (ml-infra): additional suggestion: enable auto-fallback to smaller-quantized model (realtime-infer-lite) for heavy requests until nodes are healthy. can flip a traffic-router flag.

maria (sre): agree, but prefer staged rollout: 1) keep batch reduction for 10-15m 2) if OOMs persist, flip fallback for non-SLA customers 3) if still bad, escalate to infra for emergency capacity.

sam (oncall): implementing step 1 now. monitoring.

(10 minutes later)

kai (ml-infra): observed OOMs drop to 0 in last 5m on all nodes except gpu-node-14. gpu-node-14 reboot completed; pods landing cleanly.

maria (sre): telemetry shows 99th p95 latency for realtime-infer up ~20% for affected requests but success rate back to 99.2%. pattern suggests batching was primary contributor.

pagerduty: INC-7890 status -> acknowledged -> monitoring (no longer triggered).

sam (oncall): prepping handoff to night oncall. writing blameless summary in incident ticket. planned follow-ups: adjust default batch_size based on model size, add proactive OOM alert per node when 5+ OOMs in 10m, and create playbook for fallback to quantized model.

jamal (prod-eng): request postmortem input: timeline, mitigations, customer impact, remediation owner (kai for infra changes, maria for alerts/playbook, sam for oncall runbook updates).

maria (sre): assigning owners as above. will draft postmortem.

sam (oncall): handing off to night oncall @maria in 15m. leaving incident open for monitoring.

incident-bot: NOTE: small follow-up alert configured to watch gpu-node OOM rate. will notify #eng-oncall if OOM rate rises again. :white_check_mark:
